raw_statement_token: "Let $G$ and $H$ be graphs on the same number of vertices. Their decks are **switching equivalent**, written $\\mathcal{D}(G) \\sim \\mathcal{D}(H)$, when there is a bijection between their cards sending each card to a switching-equivalent graph. A switching-equivalent class is **reconstructible** if $\\mathcal{D}(G) \\sim \\mathcal{D}(H)$ implies $G$ belongs to the switching-equivalent class of $H$. **The switching-equivalent reconstruction conjecture.** Every switching-equivalent class on at least $4$ vertices is reconstructible. The paper reports computational verification for representatives with $4\\leq n\\leq 10$ vertices, but the general assertion remains unresolved in the supplied source."
decoded_statement: Let $G$ and $H$ be graphs on the same number of vertices. Their decks are **switching equivalent**, written $\mathcal{D}(G) \sim \mathcal{D}(H)$, when there is a bijection between their cards sending each card to a switching-equivalent graph. A switching-equivalent class is **reconstructible** if $\mathcal{D}(G) \sim \mathcal{D}(H)$ implies $G$ belongs to the switching-equivalent class of $H$. **The switching-equivalent reconstruction conjecture.** Every switching-equivalent class on at least $4$ vertices is reconstructible. The paper reports computational verification for representatives with $4\leq n\leq 10$ vertices, but the general assertion remains unresolved in the supplied source.
